methods.notes: Scan actively because NUS may only be in a scan response, but do not filter or identify on that UUID. A Bangle.js-suffixed name is only a candidate: select the model manually, then confirm Android Integration ver.fw/ver.hw read-only before any write. Renamed units require the same manual path.

host_compatibility.basis: Official Bangle.js 2 documentation says Safari lacks Web Bluetooth and suggests a Web Bluetooth-capable iOS browser. Gadgetbridge/Android Integration behavior on iOS is not established by that note.
host_compatibility.notes: Native CoreBluetooth can speak NUS, but the official App Loader route needs a Web Bluetooth browser and paired-for-notifications devices may have to be disconnected before appearing. No full iOS companion verdict is claimed.

identification.notes: Default names are Bangle.js plus a short suffix shown on the watch and are candidates only, not automatic model proof. Select Bangle.js 1 or 2 manually. NUS is deliberately ABSENT from automatic identity: it is shared with Ninebot Z and many incompatible protocols. NUS may appear in a scan response, but must not activate this spec. After connecting, require Android Integration's read-only ver message and confirm hw is 1 or 2 before ANY write; otherwise stay read-only.

device.name: Espruino Bangle.js 1 and 2
device.notes:
Both watches use Nordic UART Service (NUS), not a binary smartwatch profile. Bangle.js 1 is no longer sold; Bangle.js 2 is current. Bangle.js 3 is excluded: Android Integration metadata naming it is not sufficient board/protocol evidence.
Phone/browser to watch is byte 0x10 followed by GB(<JSON object>)\n on NUS RX. Watch to phone is one JSON object per line on NUS TX, without that 0x10/GB wrapper. Fragment and coalesce arbitrarily at the UART, but do not feed ordinary Espruino console output to the Gadgetbridge JSON parser. High MTU is optional, never assumed. One active BLE connection is typical: disconnect the Web IDE before Gadgetbridge and disconnect Gadgetbridge before the App Loader/Web IDE.

procedures.basis: Official Bangle.js development and Gadgetbridge setup guides.
procedures.name: Enable BLE and Make Connectable

steps.action: Open Settings/Bluetooth, enable BLE and choose Make Connectable; leave that screen visible.
steps.expect: The watch advertises its Bangle.js suffix name.

steps.action: If a companion offers an optional bond, accept or decline it; no account or fixed PIN is needed.

exclusivity.notes: No single-bond eviction is documented; the limit is the active connection.
exclusivity.recovery: Disconnect the Web IDE/Gadgetbridge before starting the other. If bonding is stale, firmware 2v30+ Recovery offers Delete BT Pairing (Soft, then Hard for corrupted pairing flash); also forget the watch in the host OS and reconnect.

pairing.notes: Bare NUS works without a bond. Gadgetbridge optionally offers an encrypted bonded connection, reported to reconnect more reliably on modern Android. No authenticated PIN or numeric comparison is documented, so just_works is the broad mode label, not a claim of MITM protection.

unpair.clears: Bluetooth pairing information only; installed apps/files/settings remain.

procedures.indicator: Recovery menu's Delete BT Pairing entry; Soft or Hard completion.
procedures.name: Delete BT Pairing in Recovery (firmware 2v30+)

steps.action: Enter Recovery with the model's factory-reset button sequence, then select Delete BT Pairing.
steps.expect: Pairing information is removed without selecting Factory Reset.

steps.action: Try Soft first; use Hard only if pairing flash may be corrupted, then forget the watch in the host OS.

credentials.notes: No Espruino account or application token is required. App bundles fetched from banglejs.com are public and can be cached for offline installation. Optional HTTP relay can send app data off-device; keep it disabled for local-only use.
stored_on_device: Installed apps, files, settings and activity records

factory_reset.description: On firmware 2v19 and later, hold through the initial DFU text and ==== progress into Recovery, then select Factory Reset. Releasing at the first six-second mark merely reboots. On older firmware, the App Loader's Install default apps path is the documented erase/reinstall route. Clean Boot only suppresses code for one boot and is not a factory reset.
factory_reset.effect: Recovery-menu Factory Reset wipes installed data and settings and returns the watch to its factory state. App Loader Install default apps similarly erases everything and reinstalls defaults; both require setup again.

procedures.basis: Official Bangle.js 1 board guide, Recovery menu and Deleting all code.
procedures.indicator: DFU version text, ==== progress, then the Recovery menu.
procedures.name: Bangle.js 1 Recovery menu, firmware 2v19+

steps.action: Hold BTN1+BTN2+BTN3 for about six seconds until DFU text appears; release BTN1/BTN2 while keeping BTN3 held through boot.
steps.expect: The Recovery menu appears and Bluetooth is enabled.

steps.action: Release BTN3 and select Factory Reset.
steps.expect: Watch data/settings are wiped and factory defaults are restored.

steps.action: Hold the side button through DFU text and ==== while the watch boots.
steps.expect: The Recovery menu appears and Bluetooth is enabled.

steps.action: Release the button and select Factory Reset.
steps.expect: Watch data/settings are wiped and factory defaults are restored.

procedures.basis: Official board guides' pre-2v19 Deleting all code procedure.
procedures.indicator: Only the default apps remain after the erase/reinstall completes.
procedures.name: Install default apps from the App Loader (older firmware)

steps.action: Connect the App Loader, optionally after Clean Boot, and choose More, Install default apps.
steps.expect: Everything is erased and the default apps are reinstalled.

methods.description: Make the watch connectable, actively scan by the candidate name (never by NUS), select Bangle.js 1 or 2 manually, connect and subscribe to TX. For Gadgetbridge install Android Integration first; for Web IDE/App Loader enable Programmable only if code upload is intended and after the ver gate.

steps.action: On the watch, enable BLE and choose Make Connectable; install Android Integration for Gadgetbridge use.
steps.expect: The connectable screen and a Bangle.js suffix name are visible.

steps.action: Disconnect any other client, actively scan by the candidate name and select Bangle.js 1 or 2 manually; do not match on NUS.
steps.expect: The user, not the shared service UUID, chooses the model and only one client holds the link.

steps.action: Subscribe to NUS TX and retain UART bytes until each complete GB line or JSON line arrives.
steps.expect: Android Integration sends status, ver and calendar-sync messages after connection.

steps.action: Read the ver message and confirm fw is present and hw is exactly 1 or 2 before any write; otherwise remain read-only.
steps.expect: Read-only model confirmation has succeeded; no write occurs before it.

steps.action: Only after that confirmation, consider the dedicated multi-write handler; leave Programmable, Internet access, intents and file/code writes disabled unless that specific advanced operation is intended.

causes: The UUID is in a scan response; use active scanning. Also disconnect the other companion and leave the watch connectable.
troubleshooting.symptom: No NUS service appears in a passive scan.

causes: ATT notifications are fragments. Reassemble by GB()/newline boundaries rather than treating each notification as a message; negotiate high MTU only as an optimization.
troubleshooting.symptom: JSON messages are malformed after a large transfer.

causes: Install Android Integration and Messages, not the retired Gadgetbridge widget.
troubleshooting.symptom: Gadgetbridge connects but notifications do not render.

setup.notes: Raw NUS needs no account or provisioning. Full Gadgetbridge behavior requires the watch-side Android Integration app and its Messages dependency; the older Gadgetbridge widget is unmaintained. Bonding is optional, not a setup credential. This is identify-only: a user selects the Bangle model and a dedicated handler proves it read-only before offering any write.

rejoin.notes: Disconnect the old client and connect the new one. Bonding is optional; use Recovery Delete BT Pairing (2v30+) only for stale/corrupt bond state, not a reset.

steps.action: Disconnect the old phone/browser and make the watch connectable.
Connect the new client, subscribe to TX and wait for ver/status.
steps.expect: The new client receives Android Integration's version and battery messages.

testing.notes: No watch was connected or driven from this document. Protocol and recovery facts are from pinned official sources; optional Internet relay, intents, arbitrary code upload and firmware update were not exercised.

variants.notes: nRF52832, three physical buttons plus two touch zones, GPS/heart rate; no longer sold. Recovery uses BTN1+BTN2(+BTN3 held for the menu).
nRF52840, full touchscreen and one side button, GPS/heart rate/barometer; BLE-only firmware update. Recovery holds the side button.

evidence.negative_findings: No proprietary account is required. Standard Gadgetbridge has no Internet permission; the Bangle.js fork's Internet access is optional. Bangle.js 3 metadata is not enough evidence to include it. No full App Loader update algorithm is claimed.
evidence.official_board_guides: Bangle.js 1 and 2 board references supply hardware scope, button-specific reset, Recovery, pairing deletion, firmware-update and single-connection behavior. The development guide supplies Bangle.js suffix names, Make Connectable and Programmable.
evidence.official_protocol_documentation: Espruino's BLE UART guide supplies NUS and scan-response discovery. Its Gadgetbridge guide supplies the 0x10/GB phone wrapper, watch JSON lines, common message fields, optional HTTPS/intents and least-privilege switches.
evidence.open_questions: Exact App Loader file-transfer choreography, all weather field units, native iOS companion behavior, firmware-update transport details, and hardware/version-specific recorder-log compatibility need owner validation.
evidence.watch_app_source: BangleApps Android Integration 0.48 supplies connection-time status/ver/calendar behavior and the Messages dependency. Pinned commits are named in the file header; no vendor app internals are used.

common_messages.unknown_type_rule: Preserve an unknown t object for a newer handler/log it; never coerce it into a known notification, music or health entity.

entries.advanced_reason: Arbitrary code can alter/delete watch content and persist at startup.
entries.framing: Raw JavaScript over NUS RX; no 0x10/GB wrapper. Programmable must be enabled.
entries.name: arbitrary_javascript_repl

entries.advanced_reason: Can overwrite watch files/apps and break boot; use public reviewed bundles and cache them for offline reinstall.
entries.framing: App metadata declares storage/data files; Web Bluetooth writes selected files through NUS. Exact App Loader choreography is not reduced to GB JSON.
entries.name: app_loader_file_and_code_upload

entries.advanced_reason: Sends app data off-device. Requires Bangle.js Gadgetbridge Internet permission and explicit Allow Internet Access; HTTPS only, insecure:false default.
entries.direction: watch to phone, then phone to watch response
entries.name: http_relay

entries.advanced_reason: Writes arbitrary phone-side files; keep disabled unless the user approves the destination/content.
entries.framing: {t:file,n:filename,c:contents,m:a/w} JSON line; a appends, w overwrites.
entries.name: phone_file_write

entries.advanced_reason: Can launch Android activities/services and interact with other apps; requires explicit Allow Intents.
entries.name: android_intents

privileged_surfaces.least_privilege_rule: These are not needed for notifications, time/weather/music/calendar/activity sync and are not bound to ordinary entities.

reset_vs_clean_boot.clean_boot: Suppresses installed code for one boot without deleting it; useful before removing broken startup code.
reset_vs_clean_boot.delete_pairing: 2v30+ Soft/Hard pairing erase only; not a factory reset.

evaluate_javascript.advanced_reason: Executes arbitrary code on the watch and can alter/delete apps, files, settings or startup behavior. Use only reviewed code and keep a Clean Boot/Factory Reset recovery path.
evaluate_javascript.description: OPTIONAL advanced REPL input: raw JavaScript line(s), NOT GB-wrapped. Requires Programmable and a deliberate code-execution choice.
evaluate_javascript.encoding: Raw UTF-8 JavaScript including its intended line terminator; split only into the ordered UART chunks above.

find_watch_start.description: Documented Gadgetbridge find-device on: 0x10 + GB({"t":"find","n":true}) + LF; 29 bytes and therefore not one bare write.

find_watch_stop.description: Documented Gadgetbridge find-device off; 30 bytes and also requires the ordered multi-write sequence above.

write_sequence: Build one complete GB/JSON message, then write its bytes in order in chunks of at most 20; never interleave another message between chunks.
Reassemble TX notifications independently by JSON/GB line boundary. A dedicated multi-write handler is required before any command is offered.
There is no ordinary Find Watch entity or executable characteristic command in this spec.

connection_messages: About two seconds after connection Android Integration sends status with battery, ver with fw/hw, and force_calendar_sync_start via the phone-bound GB handler.
Use ver.hw to distinguish Bangle.js 1/2 when sources expose it; do not infer Bangle.js 3 from metadata.

host_to_watch.framing: 0x10 + ASCII GB( + compact JSON object + ASCII )
host_to_watch.parser:
Require the 0x10 prefix and complete GB(...)
 before decoding the enclosed single JSON object.

uart_roles.mtu: 20 bytes is a safe default chunk; higher MTU is optional and negotiated.

watch_to_host.framing: One JSON object per line, no 0x10 prefix and no GB wrapper.
watch_to_host.parser: Buffer arbitrary fragments/coalesced lines. Only lines beginning { after no leading console text are candidates; malformed JSON is rejected without consuming the next valid line.

remaining_unknowns: Exact App Loader storage/data-file transfer choreography and version-specific compatibility.
All weather/music duration field units and recorder-log edge cases across firmware versions.
A native iOS companion path with feature parity; official docs establish only the Web Bluetooth browser issue.
Firmware-update wire stack, image signing and interrupted-update recovery on each board.
Bangle.js 3 board identity and protocol; deliberately not claimed.

characteristics.name: UART RX (host writes to watch)
characteristics.notes: Documentation-only write channel. A dedicated multi-write handler must serialize each complete message into ordered <=20-byte writes and reassemble responses; bare framing cannot encode the 29/30-byte examples below. protocol_details.uart_commands is not an executable command catalogue.

characteristics.name: UART TX (watch notifies host)
characteristics.notes: Watch-to-host Gadgetbridge messages are JSON objects, one per line, with no 0x10/GB wrapper. Android Integration sends status and ver after connect and on relevant changes. Non-JSON console text belongs to the REPL, not this parser.

initialization.notes: Keep notification bytes in a stream buffer and parse complete lines only.

services.name: Nordic UART Service
services.notes: Shared NUS transport, not product identity by itself. RX is phone/browser to watch; TX is watch to phone/browser. JSON and GB lines are protocol messages, not fixed-width characteristic values.
